findings.title: Span-count cap removed from Python side while Lua now trims to 1000 silently
findings.body: The max_segment_spans check was removed from _load_segment_data, so oversized segments are no longer skipped and logged. Meanwhile the Lua script now silently zpopmin-trims sets to 1000 entries, dropping spans without any metric or log. Segments with more spans than the limit lose data silently and the max_segment_spans parameter is now dead code.

findings.title: zpopmin trims the lowest-scored (oldest) spans, not the excess
findings.body: zpopmin removes the members with the smallest scores, so when the set exceeds 1000 spans the oldest spans are discarded. This is the opposite of what is probably desired for a bounded buffer and also the span_count used is from zunionstore which returns the union cardinality, so the trim count is computed correctly but the chosen eviction policy silently drops data from the start of the segment.

findings.title: zunionstore with weights defaults sums scores; spans re-added with same payload are merged incorrectly
findings.body: zunionstore uses the default AGGREGATE SUM, so when the same payload member exists in both sets its score is summed instead of kept. Since members are the raw payload and scores are end timestamps, duplicate spans moved between sets get their timestamp doubled, corrupting eviction ordering.

findings.title: Span payload timestamp used as sort score makes ZADD of duplicate payloads ineffective
findings.body: process_spans builds a dict {payload: end_timestamp} for zadd; if two identical payloads occur in a batch the dict dedupes them, which is fine, but the pipeline previously used sadd. Score-based sets also change the flush_segments/_load_segment_data contract (zscan returns (member, score) tuples) without any migration for segments already stored as Redis sets, causing WRONGTYPE errors on rolling deploy.

findings.title: Negative offsets now reach the queryset slice path for is_prev cursors
findings.body: start_offset is set to offset without clamping when cursor.is_prev, so a negative offset from a crafted cursor produces a negative slice index. Django raises an error for negative slicing (ValueError 'Negative indexing is not supported'), turning a bad cursor into a 500 instead of a 400 BadPaginationError. The 'Performance optimization' comments are misleading and the behavior change is not tested.

findings.title: Advanced-feature negative offset path lets authorized-looking requests bypass bounds
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows negative cursor offsets when enable_advanced_features is set, slicing the queryset with negative start indices. The comment claims permissions are checked at queryset level, but the queryset is only filtered by organization, not by pagination bounds, so arbitrary negative offsets expose rows beyond normal page bounds and can trigger Django negative-indexing errors. This adds an unreviewed data-access path.

findings.title: Advanced pagination gated by query parameter and privilege without tests
findings.body: The optimized paginator is enabled by a client-supplied query parameter for superusers or global-access members, and the endpoint now differs in pagination behavior. There is no test covering this branch, and the 'enable_advanced' flag unlocks the negative-offset path in the paginator, expanding what an admin request can read in audit logs.

findings.title: Trailing whitespace and duplicated paginate call
findings.body: Lines with trailing whitespace were introduced and the paginate call is duplicated across both branches, which makes future changes error-prone; the branch only differs by paginator class and one kwarg.

findings.title: Comment claims a performance optimization that the constructor does not implement
findings.body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for efficient reverse pagination, but the code only does int(offset) and the behavior change is elsewhere. The comment misrepresents the code and the risky negative-offset semantics are not documented in the cursor contract.

findings.title: KeyError if message lacks end_timestamp_precise
findings.body: val['end_timestamp_precise'] is accessed directly; any span payload without this field now raises KeyError and crashes the batch processing step, whereas the other fields are validated as needed. The schema cast does not validate at runtime, so this should be val.get with handling or a documented requirement.

findings.title: No tests for span-count eviction at 1000 or the removed max_segment_spans skip
findings.body: The PR adds zpopmin eviction at 1000 spans and removes the max_segment_spans rejection, but no test exercises either behavior. Regressions in the eviction boundary or the Lua return path would go unnoticed.
